level.description: Effort level the review ran at

findings.description: Verified findings, most-severe first; empty if none survived

file.description: Repo-relative path of the file the finding is in

short_summary.description: Compressed label for compact UI (≤60 chars): the claim alone, no rationale or consequence clause

category.description: Short kebab-case slug of the finding type, e.g. "correctness", "simplification", "efficiency", "test-coverage"

verdict.description: Set when a verify pass ran; absent on inline-only reviews

outcome.description: Set ONLY when re-reporting after applying fixes: what happened to this finding

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a listing from the system with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in a message from the system. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a message from the system confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a message from the system confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

A call a usage limit refused, or one still running when the run stopped, usually runs again without ending reuse: finished calls after it still come from cache. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

library only). Read the code first: `README.md`, `tabula/engine.py` and `tests/`. It has four commands today (`show`,

default) says how the result table is printed; a mistake in a file or in what I asked for prints
`tabula: <message>` on standard error and exits 1, with nothing on standard output; a command line that is not shaped
right (a missing argument, an unknown option, a condition with no operator) exits 2. A "row N" in a message counts the
data rows of the file from 1, the header not counted, in the order of the file (not the sorted order). Cell values are
text; a **number** is what `to_decimal` accepts (an optional sign, digits, an optional decimal point; no exponent, no
thousands marks). All arithmetic is exact (`Decimal`), never floating point. A column named in a request that the file
does not have is a mistake in the request (exit 1, the message names the column).

Two options are new and are read by one command each, but they are accepted on any command line, before or after the
command: `--kind inner|left` and `--keep first|last`, each as `--opt value` or `--opt=value`. Any other value is a
usage error (exit 2).

## sort

`tabula sort FILE KEY...` prints the rows sorted by the first KEY, ties by the second, and so on. A KEY is a column
name, optionally followed by the modifiers `:num` (compare as numbers, not as text) and `:desc` (largest first), in
either order (`price:num:desc`, `price:desc:num`). Text compares by code point (so `B` sorts before `a`). The sort is
stable: rows that tie on every key keep the order of the file, also with `:desc`. With `:num`, a cell that is not a
number is a mistake: `FILE: row N: column 'price': 'abc' is not a number`. A modifier given twice in one KEY is a usage

# Commands

`tabula [--format text|csv|json] COMMAND ARGS...` reads CSV files (UTF-8, an optional byte order mark, LF or CRLF) and prints
a table. Every command returns a `Table`; `--format` says how it is printed (text by default). A mistake in a file or in a
request exits 1 with `tabula: <message>` on standard error; a command line that is not shaped right exits 2.

## show

`tabula show FILE` prints the whole table. Blank lines in the file are ignored. A row with more or fewer fields than the
header is a mistake that names the file and the line (`t.csv: line 3: expected 2 fields, found 1`).

## head

`tabula head FILE N` prints the header and the first N rows. N is a whole number (zero is fine); anything else is a usage
error.

## cols

`tabula cols FILE` prints one row per column with two columns, `position` (from 1) and `column`.

## apply

`tabula apply FILE COLUMN TRANSFORM...` runs each TRANSFORM, left to right, over every value of one column and prints the
whole table. A transform is `name` or `name:ARG`; the list is in `docs/transforms.md`. A value a transform cannot take is
a mistake that names the file and the row (`t.csv: row 2: 'abc' is not a number`). Rows count from 1, the header not
counted.

"""tabula.engine -- the table model, the transforms, the output formats and the command line.

This is the one module every command lives in. A command is a function `cmd_NAME(args, opts)` that gets the
positional arguments (a list of strings) and the options (a dict) and returns a Table, which `main` then prints in the
format asked for (`--format text|csv|json`, text by default). A mistake in a file or in a request raises TabulaError
(exit status 1); a command line that is not shaped right raises UsageError (exit status 2).
"""
import csv
import io
import json
import re
import sys
import unicodedata
from decimal import Decimal, InvalidOperation, ROUND_HALF_UP, ROUND_FLOOR, ROUND_CEILING, ROUND_DOWN, getcontext

from .errors import TabulaError, UsageError

PROG = "tabula"
FORMATS = ("text", "csv", "json")
getcontext().prec = 60

NUMBER = re.compile(r"[+-]?(?:\d+(?:\.\d*)?|\.\d+)")


# --- numbers -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

def to_decimal(text):
    """The Decimal a cell holds, or None when it is not a plain decimal number (no exponent, no thousands marks)."""
    text = text.strip()
    if not NUMBER.fullmatch(text):
        return None
    try:
        return Decimal(text)
    except InvalidOperation:
        return None


def fmt_decimal(number):
    """A Decimal as plain text: no exponent, no negative zero."""
    text = format(number, "f")
    if text.startswith("-") and not text.strip("-0."):
        text = text[1:]
    return text


def _need_number(value):
    number = to_decimal(value)
    if number is None:
        raise TabulaError("%r is not a number" % value)
    return number


def _need_count(arg, name):
    if arg is None or not arg.isdigit():
        raise TabulaError("%s needs a whole number argument, got %r" % (name, arg))
    return int(arg)


def _need_decimal_arg(arg, name):
    number = None if arg is None else to_decimal(arg)
    if number is None:
        raise TabulaError("%s needs a number argument, got %r" % (name, arg))
    return number


def _no_arg(name, arg):
    if arg is not None:
        raise TabulaError("%s takes no argument, got %r" % (name, arg))


def _need_text(arg, name):
    if arg is None:
        raise TabulaError("%s needs an argument" % name)
    return arg


# --- the table -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

class Table:
    """Column names and rows of strings. `source` names where it came from, for messages."""

    def __init__(self, columns, rows, source="<table>"):
        self.columns = list(columns)
        self.rows = [list(r) for r in rows]
        self.source = source

    def __len__(self):
        return len(self.rows)

    def index(self, name):
        """Position of a column; TabulaError when there is none."""
        try:
            return self.columns.index(name)
        except ValueError:
            raise TabulaError("%s: no column %r (columns: %s)" % (self.source, name, ", ".join(self.columns)))

    def column(self, name):
        at = self.index(name)
        return [row[at] for row in self.rows]

    def dicts(self):
        return [dict(zip(self.columns, row)) for row in self.rows]

    def with_rows(self, rows, columns=None):
        return Table(self.columns if columns is None else columns, rows, self.source)


def parse_text(text, source):
    """CSV text into a Table. Blank lines are ignored; every row must have as many fields as the header."""
    if text.startswith("﻿"):
        text = text[1:]
    reader = csv.reader(io.StringIO(text, newline=""))
    columns, rows = None, []
    try:
        for fields in reader:
            if not fields:
                continue
            if columns is None:
                for name in fields:
                    if not name.strip():
                        raise TabulaError("%s: line %d: empty column name" % (source, reader.line_num))
                if len(set(fields)) != len(fields):
                    raise TabulaError("%s: line %d: duplicate column name" % (source, reader.line_num))
                columns = fields
                continue
            if len(fields) != len(columns):
                raise TabulaError("%s: line %d: expected %d fields, found %d"
                                  % (source, reader.line_num, len(columns), len(fields)))
            rows.append(fields)
    except csv.Error as exc:
        raise TabulaError("%s: line %d: %s" % (source, reader.line_num, exc))
    if columns is None:
        raise TabulaError("%s: no header line" % source)
    return Table(columns, rows, source)


def load(path):
    """Read a CSV file (UTF-8, optional byte order mark, LF or CRLF) into a Table."""
    try:
        with open(path, "rb") as fh:
            raw = fh.read()
    except OSError as exc:
        raise TabulaError("%s: cannot read: %s" % (path, exc.strerror or exc))
    try:
        text = raw.decode("utf-8")
    except UnicodeDecodeError:
        raise TabulaError("%s: not valid UTF-8" % path)
    return parse_text(text, path)


# --- output --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

def render_text(table):
    cells = [table.columns] + table.rows
    widths = [max(len(row[i]) for row in cells) for i in range(len(table.columns))]
    lines = ["  ".join(cell.ljust(width) for cell, width in zip(row, widths)).rstrip() for row in cells]
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def render_csv(table):
    out = io.StringIO()
    writer = csv.writer(out, lineterminator="\n")
    writer.writerow(table.columns)
    writer.writerows(table.rows)
    return out.getvalue()


def render_json(table):
    return json.dumps(table.dicts(), ensure_ascii=False) + "\n"


RENDERERS = {"text": render_text, "csv": render_csv, "json": render_json}


def render(table, fmt="text"):
    return RENDERERS[fmt](table)


# --- transforms: one small function each, `name` or `name:ARG` in `apply` ----------------------------------------


def t_upper(value, arg=None):
    """The value in upper case.

    Example: upper applied to '  Héllo, World 42 "x" ' gives '  HÉLLO, WORLD 42 "X" '.
    An argument that is missing or of the wrong kind is a TabulaError, not a guess.
    """
    _no_arg("upper", arg)
    return value.upper()


def t_lower(value, arg=None):
    """The value in lower case.

    Example: lower applied to '  Héllo, World 42 "x" ' gives '  héllo, world 42 "x" '.
    An argument that is missing or of the wrong kind is a TabulaError, not a guess.
    """
    _no_arg("lower", arg)
    return value.lower()


def t_title(value, arg=None):
    """Each word capitalised.

    Example: title applied to '  Héllo, World 42 "x" ' gives '  Héllo, World 42 "X" '.
    An argument that is missing or of the wrong kind is a TabulaError, not a guess.
    """
    _no_arg("title", arg)
    return value.title()


def t_capitalize(value, arg=None):
    """The first letter upper, the rest lower.

    Example: capitalize applied to '  Héllo, World 42 "x" ' gives '  héllo, world 42 "x" '.
    An argument that is missing or of the wrong kind is a TabulaError, not a guess.
    """
    _no_arg("capitalize", arg)
    return value.capitalize()


def t_swapcase(value, arg=None):
    """Upper and lower case swapped.

    Example: swapcase applied to '  Héllo, World 42 "x" ' gives '  hÉLLO, wORLD 42 "X" '.
    An argument that is missing or of the wrong kind is a TabulaError, not a guess.
    """
    _no_arg("swapcase", arg)
    return value.swapcase()


def t_strip(value, arg=None):
    """Without leading and trailing whitespace.

    Example: strip applied to '  Héllo, World 42 "x" ' gives 'Héllo, World 42 "x"'.
    An argument that is missing or of the wrong kind is a TabulaError, not a guess.
    """
    _no_arg("strip", arg)
    return value.strip()


def t_lstrip(value, arg=None):
    """Without leading whitespace.

    Example: lstrip applied to '  Héllo, World 42 "x" ' gives 'Héllo, World 42 "x" '.
    An argument that is missing or of the wrong kind is a TabulaError, not a guess.
    """
    _no_arg("lstrip", arg)
    return value.lstrip()


def t_rstrip(value, arg=None):
    """Without trailing whitespace.

    Example: rstrip applied to '  Héllo, World 42 "x" ' gives '  Héllo, World 42 "x"'.
    An argument that is missing or of the wrong kind is a TabulaError, not a guess.
    """
    _no_arg("rstrip", arg)
    return value.rstrip()


def t_reverse(value, arg=None):
    """The characters in reverse order.

    Example: reverse applied to '  Héllo, World 42 "x" ' gives ' "x" 24 dlroW ,olléH  '.
    An argument that is missing or of the wrong kind is a TabulaError, not a guess.
    """
    _no_arg("reverse", arg)
    return value[::-1]


def t_squeeze(value, arg=None):
    """Runs of whitespace collapsed to one space.

    Example: squeeze applied to '  Héllo, World 42 "x" ' gives 'Héllo, World 42 "x"'.
    An argument that is missing or of the wrong kind is a TabulaError, not a guess.
    """
    _no_arg("squeeze", arg)
    return ' '.join(value.split())


def t_nospace(value, arg=None):
    """All whitespace removed.

    Example: nospace applied to '  Héllo, World 42 "x" ' gives 'Héllo,World42"x"'.
    An argument that is missing or of the wrong kind is a TabulaError, not a guess.
    """
    _no_arg("nospace", arg)
    return ''.join(value.split())


def t_digits(value, arg=None):
    """Only the digits.

    Example: digits applied to '  Héllo, World 42 "x" ' gives '42'.
    An argument that is missing or of the wrong kind is a TabulaError, not a guess.
    """
    _no_arg("digits", arg)
    return ''.join(c for c in value if c.isdigit())


def t_letters(value, arg=None):
    """Only the letters.

    Example: letters applied to '  Héllo, World 42 "x" ' gives 'HélloWorldx'.
    An argument that is missing or of the wrong kind is a TabulaError, not a guess.
    """
    _no_arg("letters", arg)
    return ''.join(c for c in value if c.isalpha())


def t_alnum(value, arg=None):
    """Only letters and digits.

    Example: alnum applied to '  Héllo, World 42 "x" ' gives 'HélloWorld42x'.
    An argument that is missing or of the wrong kind is a TabulaError, not a guess.
    """
    _no_arg("alnum", arg)
    return ''.join(c for c in value if c.isalnum())


def t_punct_free(value, arg=None):
    """Punctuation removed.

    Example: punct_free applied to '  Héllo, World 42 "x" ' gives '  Héllo World 42 x '.
    An argument that is missing or of the wrong kind is a TabulaError, not a guess.
    """
    _no_arg("punct_free", arg)
    return re.sub(r'[^\w\s]', '', value)


def t_slug(value, arg=None):
    """Lower case words joined by dashes.

    Example: slug applied to '  Héllo, World 42 "x" ' gives 'h-llo-world-42-x'.
    An argument that is missing or of the wrong kind is a TabulaError, not a guess.
    """
    _no_arg("slug", arg)
    return re.sub(r'[^a-z0-9]+', '-', value.lower()).strip('-')

class CliTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def run_cli(self, *argv, files=None):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
            for k, v in (files or {}).items():
                with open(os.path.join(d, k), 'w', encoding='utf-8', newline='') as fh:
                    fh.write(v)
            env = dict(os.environ, PYTHONPATH=os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), '..'))
            p = subprocess.run([sys.executable, '-m', 'tabula'] + list(argv), cwd=d, env=env, capture_output=True, text=True)
            return p.returncode, p.stdout, p.stderr

    def test_commands(self):
        f = {'t.csv': 'name,qty\nax,3\nby,10\ncz,7\n'}
        for argv, rc, out in [(('show', 't.csv'), 0, 'name  qty\nax    3\nby    10\ncz    7\n'),
                              (('head', 't.csv', '1'), 0, 'name  qty\nax    3\n'),
                              (('--format', 'csv', 'cols', 't.csv'), 0, 'position,column\n1,name\n2,qty\n'),
                              (('apply', 't.csv', 'qty', 'add:1', 'mul:2', '--format=csv'), 0, 'name,qty\nax,8\nby,22\ncz,16\n'),
                              (('apply', 't.csv', 'name', 'upper', '--format', 'json'), 0, '[{"name": "AX", "qty": "3"}, {"name": "BY", "qty": "10"}, {"name": "CZ", "qty": "7"}]\n'),
                              (('show', 'missing.csv'), 1, ''), (('apply', 't.csv', 'nope', 'upper'), 1, ''),
                              (('apply', 't.csv', 'name', 'add:1'), 1, ''), (('bogus',), 2, ''), ((), 2, ''), (('show', '--wat', 't.csv'), 2, '')]:
            with self.subTest(argv):
                got = self.run_cli(*argv, files=f)
                self.assertEqual((got[0], got[1]), (rc, out))
                self.assertEqual(bool(got[2]), rc != 0)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    unittest.main()

def t_contains(value, arg=None):
    """Yes when the value contains the argument.

    Example: contains:- applied to 'alpha-beta-gamma' gives 'yes'.
    An argument that is missing or of the wrong kind is a TabulaError, not a guess.
    """
    arg = _need_text(arg, "contains")
    return 'yes' if arg in value else 'no'


def t_icontains(value, arg=None):
    """Yes when it contains the argument, case aside.

    Example: icontains:- applied to 'alpha-beta-gamma' gives 'yes'.
    An argument that is missing or of the wrong kind is a TabulaError, not a guess.
    """
    arg = _need_text(arg, "icontains")
    return 'yes' if arg.lower() in value.lower() else 'no'


def t_count_of(value, arg=None):
    """How many times the argument occurs.

    Example: count_of:- applied to 'alpha-beta-gamma' gives '2'.
    An argument that is missing or of the wrong kind is a TabulaError, not a guess.
    """
    arg = _need_text(arg, "count_of")
    return str(value.count(arg)) if arg else '0'

## Problem Statement

`tabula` (Python ≥3.9, standard library only, everything in `tabula/engine.py`) can only show, head, list columns and apply transforms to a CSV file. The user needs seven more table commands — `sort`, `filter`, `group`, `join`, `pivot`, `dedupe`, `stats` — that behave like the existing four: same output formats, same error and exit-status rules, exact `Decimal` arithmetic.

## Solution

Add seven commands to `tabula/engine.py`, each a `cmd_NAME(args, opts)` returning a `Table` with one entry in `COMMANDS`, plus two new global options `--kind inner|left` (read by `join`) and `--keep first|last` (read by `dedupe`). Each command gets `tests/test_NAME.py`, a section in `docs/commands.md` (after `apply`, in the order sort, filter, group, join, pivot, dedupe, stats, written like the existing sections) and its name in the README command list. Existing behaviour (the four commands, their output, exit statuses, `pip install .` giving `tabula` and `import tabula`) must not change; the existing 109 tests keep passing.

## User Stories

1. As a user, I run `tabula sort FILE KEY...` with keys like `price:num:desc` to order rows, stably, by one or more columns.
2. As a user, I run `tabula filter FILE CONDITION...` (`price>=10`, `city==Leeds`, `name~gnome`) to keep matching rows.
3. As a user, I run `tabula group FILE BY AGGREGATE...` (`count`, `sum:qty`, `min:`, `max:`, `mean:`) to summarise by a column.
4. As a user, I run `tabula join LEFT RIGHT KEY [--kind inner|left]` to combine two files.
5. As a user, I run `tabula pivot FILE ROW COLUMN VALUE` to spread a column's values into columns with summed cells.
6. As a user, I run `tabula dedupe FILE KEY... [--keep first|last]` to drop duplicate rows.
7. As a user, I run `tabula stats FILE COLUMN...` to get count/min/max/mean/median per column.
8. As a user, every command honours `--format text|csv|json`, prints `tabula: <message>` on stderr and nothing on stdout with exit 1 for a mistake in a file or request, and exits 2 for a badly shaped command line.

## Implementation Decisions

### Decomposition
Exactly **seven child issues, one per command** (no separate groundwork issue, no `## Blocked by` between them — they are independent). The shared groundwork below is part of whichever child lands first; every later child rebases and **reuses** it, never re-implements it. Children touch the same lines (`COMMANDS`, `parse_args`, docs, README): resolve conflicts by keeping both sides, keeping docs sections and README entries in the order sort, filter, group, join, pivot, dedupe, stats.

### Shared groundwork — finish the module's conventions, do not add a second way
- **Options: one table, one loop.** Replace the hand-coded `--format` branch in `parse_args` with a single table, e.g. `OPTIONS = {"format": FORMATS, "kind": ("inner", "left"), "keep": ("first", "last")}` with defaults `{"format": "text", "kind": "inner", "keep": "first"}` always present in `opts`. One code path handles `--opt value` and `--opt=value` for every option, before or after the command, with today's messages generalised (`--NAME needs a value`, `--NAME must be one of a, b, got 'x'`; exit 2). `--format` behaviour and messages stay byte-identical. Options are accepted on any command line; only `join` reads `kind`, only `dedupe` reads `keep`.
- **Argument counts: one helper.** Extend `_need_args(args, count, usage)` with a "count or more" form (e.g. `_need_args(args, count, usage, more=True)`), and switch `cmd_apply`'s hand-rolled `len(args) < 3` check to it (message unchanged). Usage messages are `usage: tabula <the COMMANDS usage string>`.
- **Numbers in cells: reuse `_need_number`.** One helper wraps it with the row and column, e.g. `_cell_number(table, row_no, column, value)` raising `TabulaError("%s: row %d: column %r: %s" % (table.source, row_no, column, exc))` → `t.csv: row 3: column 'price': 'abc' is not a number`. Row numbers are the 1-based position in the file (header not counted), never the sorted position. `apply`'s existing message stays as it is.
- **Number output: reuse `fmt_decimal`** for sum/min/max/pivot cells (no `+`, no exponent, `10.50` stays `10.50`, no negative zero). Two-decimal half-up output (`mean`, `median`) goes through one rounding helper (e.g. `_round_half_up(number, places)` using `quantize(..., ROUND_HALF_UP)`), and `t_round_to`/`t_round0` are switched to the same helper (their outputs unchanged). Always two decimals: `5.00`, `2.25`.
- **Columns: `Table.index(name)`** for every column named in a request (its message already names the file and column; exit 1). Results built with `Table(...)`/`table.with_rows(...)`, keeping `source`.
- **Case-insensitive contains: the same rule as `t_icontains`** (`value.lower()` / `arg.lower()`); share it, do not write a second rule.
- A result table with no rows still prints its header (true of the renderers today).

### Per-command decisions (where the brief leaves room)
- **sort**: KEY splits on `:`; the first part is the column, each further part must be `num` or `desc`. Unknown modifier, a modifier twice, or an empty column part → usage error (2). No KEY → usage error. Text compares by code point (plain `str` ordering). Stable, also with `:desc` (do not implement desc by reversing the sorted list; e.g. sort once per key from last to first with `reverse=` on a stable sort, which keeps ties in file order). `:num` on a non-number (including empty) → `FILE: row N: column 'C': 'x' is not a number`, N the file row.
- **filter**: operator = earliest position in the argument; at equal position the longer one (`>=`, `<=`, `==`, `!=` before `>`, `<`). No operator or empty column → usage error (2). Empty VALUE is allowed. For all ops but `~`: if both `to_decimal(cell)` and `to_decimal(value)` are numbers compare as `Decimal`, else as text by code point. `~`: case-insensitive containment as `t_icontains`. All conditions must hold. Unknown column → exit 1.
- **group**: output columns `BY` then each aggregate as written with `:` → `_`. `count` takes no column; `sum|min|max|mean` need `:COLUMN`; anything else (unknown name, `count:x`, `sum` or `sum:` with no column) or the same aggregate twice → usage error (2). Missing column → exit 1. `count` printed as a whole number. If the result would contain a column name twice (e.g. BY column named `count` with aggregate `count`, or `sum_qty`), that is a mistake (exit 1, message names the column).
- **join**: exactly three args. KEY missing in either file → exit 1 naming that file. Result columns: LEFT's, then RIGHT's minus KEY, a RIGHT name already in LEFT gets `_right`; if names still collide → exit 1 naming the column. Inner (default): per LEFT row, one row per matching RIGHT row in RIGHT order. Left: unmatched LEFT row once with empty strings for the RIGHT columns.
- **pivot**: exactly four args; ROW == COLUMN → usage error (2). Empty COLUMN value → `FILE: row N: column 'C': empty value`; a COLUMN value equal to the ROW column's name → exit 1, `FILE: row N: column 'C': value 'X' is the name of the row column`. Sums exact, printed with `fmt_decimal`; missing pair → `0`. Non-number VALUE → the `_cell_number` message. (Whitespace-only counts as empty only where the brief says so — in `stats`; in pivot "empty" means the empty string.)
- **dedupe**: at least one KEY; text equality across all KEY columns; `--keep first` (default) / `--keep last`; survivors in file order.
- **stats**: at least one COLUMN; output columns `column,count,min,max,mean,median`, one row per COLUMN in the order asked (repeats allowed). Cells with `value.strip() == ""` are skipped; every other cell must be a number (`_cell_number` message). Median of an even count = exact mean of the two middle values, then rounded. No numbers → `COLUMN,0,,,,`.

## Testing Decisions
- One `tests/test_NAME.py` per command, `unittest`, in the style of `CliTests` in `tests/test_engine.py` (run `python -m tabula` in a temp dir via subprocess; assert exit status, exact stdout, stderr non-empty iff failure, stdout empty on failure). Cover text, csv and json output at least once per command, every error path named in this PRD (exit 1 vs 2), and the edge cases in the acceptance criteria.
- Shared groundwork is tested where it lands (option parsing forms `--kind left`, `--kind=left`, before/after the command, bad value → 2, missing value → 2; `--format` unchanged).
- `python -m unittest discover tests` passes after every merge; `pip install .` in a fresh venv gives a working `tabula` and `import tabula`.

## Out of Scope
- Any change to the four existing commands' output, messages or exit statuses, or to the transforms' behaviour.
- New dependencies, a package split, or moving code out of `tabula/engine.py`.
- Floating point anywhere; exponent or thousands-separator numbers.
- Multi-column join keys, outer/right joins, other aggregates, regex filters.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `--kind inner|left` and `--keep first|last` accepted on any command line, before or after the command, as `--opt v` or `--opt=v`; another value or a missing value → exit 2; handled by the same single option table/loop as `--format`.
- [ ] `--format` and the four existing commands behave exactly as before; the original 109 tests pass unchanged.
- [ ] No second way to do what the module already does: one option loop, one arg-count helper (`apply` uses it), `_need_number`/`to_decimal` for numbers, `fmt_decimal` for number output, one half-up rounding helper (shared with `round_to`/`round0`), `Table.index` for columns, `t_icontains`'s rule for `~`.
- [ ] Non-number messages read `FILE: row N: column 'C': 'x' is not a number` with N the 1-based file row.
- [ ] `sort`: multi-key, `:num`/`:desc` in either order, code-point text order (`B` before `a`), stable also with `:desc`; duplicate/unknown modifier or no KEY → 2.
- [ ] `filter`: all seven operators, earliest-then-longest operator rule, numeric compare when both sides are numbers (`10 > 9`, `1.0 == 1`), `~` case-insensitive; no operator / empty column / no CONDITION → 2; no rows left still prints the header.
- [ ] `group`: first-appearance order, aggregate column names `sum_qty` etc., sum/min/max via `fmt_decimal` (`10.50` stays), mean half-up with two decimals; unknown/duplicate aggregate or none → 2.
- [ ] `join`: column naming with `_right`, irreducible duplicate name → 1, inner and left kinds in the specified row order, exactly three args.
- [ ] `pivot`: first-appearance order of rows and columns, exact sums, `0` for absent pairs, ROW == COLUMN → 2, empty COLUMN value and value equal to ROW name → 1, exactly four args.
- [ ] `dedupe`: keep first (default) / last, survivors in file order, at least one KEY.
- [ ] `stats`: columns `column,count,min,max,mean,median`, whitespace-only cells skipped, even-count median exact, no numbers → `COLUMN,0` and four empty cells, at least one COLUMN.
- [ ] Unknown column in any request → exit 1 naming the column; every failure prints only `tabula: <message>` on stderr, nothing on stdout.
- [ ] Each command has `tests/test_NAME.py`, a `docs/commands.md` section (order: sort, filter, group, join, pivot, dedupe, stats, after `apply`) and an entry in the README command list; `COMMANDS` usage text lists it.
- [ ] Standard library only, Python 3.9 compatible, all arithmetic `Decimal`.

- **Columns: `Table.index(name)`** for every column named in a request (its message already names the file and column; exit 1). Results built with `Table(...)`/`table.with_rows(...)`, keeping `source`.
- **Case-insensitive contains: the same rule as `t_icontains`** (`value.lower()` / `arg.lower()`); share it, do not write a second rule.
- A result table with no rows still prints its header (true of the renderers today).

### Per-command decisions (where the brief leaves room)
- **sort**: KEY splits on `:`; the first part is the column, each further part must be `num` or `desc`. Unknown modifier, a modifier twice, or an empty column part → usage error (2). No KEY → usage error. Text compares by code point (plain `str` ordering). Stable, also with `:desc` (do not implement desc by reversing the sorted list; e.g. sort once per key from last to first with `reverse=` on a stable sort, which keeps ties in file order). `:num` on a non-number (including empty) → `FILE: row N: column 'C': 'x' is not a number`, N the file row.
- **filter**: operator = earliest position in the argument; at equal position the longer one (`>=`, `<=`, `==`, `!=` before `>`, `<`). No operator or empty column → usage error (2). Empty VALUE is allowed. For all ops but `~`: if both `to_decimal(cell)` and `to_decimal(value)` are numbers compare as `Decimal`, else as text by code point. `~`: case-insensitive containment as `t_icontains`. All conditions must hold. Unknown column → exit 1.
- **group**: output columns `BY` then each aggregate as written with `:` → `_`. `count` takes no column; `sum|min|max|mean` need `:COLUMN`; anything else (unknown name, `count:x`, `sum` or `sum:` with no column) or the same aggregate twice → usage error (2). Missing column → exit 1. `count` printed as a whole number. If the result would contain a column name twice (e.g. BY column named `count` with aggregate `count`, or `sum_qty`), that is a mistake (exit 1, message names the column).
- **join**: exactly three args. KEY missing in either file → exit 1 naming that file. Result columns: LEFT's, then RIGHT's minus KEY, a RIGHT name already in LEFT gets `_right`; if names still collide → exit 1 naming the column. Inner (default): per LEFT row, one row per matching RIGHT row in RIGHT order. Left: unmatched LEFT row once with empty strings for the RIGHT columns.
- **pivot**: exactly four args; ROW == COLUMN → usage error (2). Empty COLUMN value → `FILE: row N: column 'C': empty value`; a COLUMN value equal to the ROW column's name → exit 1, `FILE: row N: column 'C': value 'X' is the name of the row column`. Sums exact, printed with `fmt_decimal`; missing pair → `0`. Non-number VALUE → the `_cell_number` message. (Whitespace-only counts as empty only where the brief says so — in `stats`; in pivot "empty" means the empty string.)
- **dedupe**: at least one KEY; text equality across all KEY columns; `--keep first` (default) / `--keep last`; survivors in file order.
- **stats**: at least one COLUMN; output columns `column,count,min,max,mean,median`, one row per COLUMN in the order asked (repeats allowed). Cells with `value.strip() == ""` are skipped; every other cell must be a number (`_cell_number` message). Median of an even count = exact mean of the two middle values, then rounded. No numbers → `COLUMN,0,,,,`.

PRD: OPEN prd,reviewed | open: 19,1
Reviewed: all acceptance criteria met.

The full suite passes at 274fb27: 177 tests under Python 3.13 and again under Python 3.9.25, with the original `tests/test_engine.py` unchanged. `pip install .` in a fresh venv gives a working `tabula` command and `import tabula`. I also ran the CLI by hand against every rule of the original request: sort, filter, group, join, pivot, dedupe and stats, every error path (exit 1 versus 2, the message wording, nothing on stdout), and the `--kind`/`--keep` forms. I then tried the awkward inputs. A byte order mark, invalid UTF-8, CRLF and lone-CR line endings, a form feed or U+2028 inside a field, and empty option values all behaved correctly. So did 5000-digit numbers through sort, filter, group, pivot and stats, output piped to `head -1`, and output sent to `/dev/full`. All of these matched the specification.

One blocking finding is filed as #19. Compiled `__pycache__/*.pyc` files have been committed since the sort PR and there is no `.gitignore`, so every test run dirties the working tree. This is repository hygiene only; command behaviour is not affected.

Review notes (non-blocking, within the direct limits, so no issue was filed):
- **[non-blocking] docs/commands.md intro line does not mention --kind and --keep** (docs/commands.md)
  - Repro: sed -n 3p docs/commands.md
  - Expected: The synopsis matches README.md: tabula [--format text|csv|json] [--kind inner|left] [--keep first|last] COMMAND ARGS...
  - Actual: Line 3 reads: tabula [--format text|csv|json] COMMAND ARGS...
  - Detail: This is wording only. The join and dedupe sections already describe --kind and --keep.
- A column whose name starts with `-` (for example `-x`) cannot be named on the command line: `tabula stats t.csv -x` exits 2 with `unknown option -x`. This option parsing was already there before this work, and the original request says that general behaviour "stays as it is", so it is not filed.
